standard_prerequisites: Loop spaces: for a type A with basepoint a, the type of loops x = x, and the second loop space of 2-dimensional loops between identity loops.
Path concatenation and inversion with their definitional behaviour on refl.
The unit laws for path concatenation (right and left unit laws as elements of iterated identity types), stated by the retained context.
The induction principle for identity types (path induction) with its conversion rule.
core_obligations: Define whiskering operations on 2-paths: right whiskering of a 2-path against a 1-path by induction on the 1-path, and left whiskering by induction on the other 1-path, with the author's explicit definitions via the unit laws.
Define the horizontal composition of 2-paths from the two whiskerings, and note the mirrored alternative definition.

Show that when all base 1-paths are reflexivity, horizontal composition reduces definitionally to ordinary concatenation, so alpha hconcat beta equals alpha concat beta, and the mirrored version equals beta concat alpha.
Show the two horizontal compositions agree by double path induction reducing everything to reflexivity, and conclude commutativity: alpha concat beta equals beta concat alpha.
proof_roadmap: Set up the whiskering: for alpha in p = q and a 1-path r in b = c, define alpha right-whiskered with r in (p concat r) = (q concat r) by path induction on r, giving the explicit formula with the right unit law from the retained context; similarly define left whiskering with its formula using the left unit law.
Define horizontal composition alpha hconcat beta as (alpha right-whisker r) concatenated with (q left-whisker beta), a 2-path in p concat r = q concat s.

Specialize to the second loop space: when a, b, c are all the basepoint and p, q, r, s are all reflexivity, the definitions reduce definitionally so that alpha hconcat beta equals alpha concat beta; by symmetry the mirrored horizontal composition hconcat-prime equals beta concat alpha.
Prove the interchange identity: alpha hconcat beta equals alpha hconcat-prime beta by induction on alpha and beta and then on the remaining 1-paths, reducing everything to reflexivity.
Chain the three identifications to conclude alpha concat beta equals beta concat alpha.
difficulty_reason: The full Eckmann-Hilton argument: two whiskering constructions with explicit unit-law corrections, a definitional reduction on the double loop space, an interchange law proven by nested induction, and the final commutativity chain.
